Builds .aletheore/air.json, .aletheore/air.toon, and history snapshots.

Tree-sitter and git history produce air.json and air.toon. No LLM in the scan path and no account. A scan makes dependency advisory and license lookups and checks for a newer release, each of which can be turned off, and sends a crash report only if the CLI itself crashes.
AIR: $29.99/month. Up to 3 team seats, $18 of AI credit a month. Everything in Flash plus the managed dashboard.

Some optional commands send data to an LLM provider you configure, using your own API key. An AI-assisted audit command sends evidence, not source code. Asking a question with aletheore query answer does send code: your question and the most relevant chunks of your source code go to that provider.

Use your own provider locally, or run a managed audit with an Aletheore API token.

If the CLI itself crashes, it sends a crash report to our error-tracking provider, Sentry: the exception details and stack trace, the Aletheore, operating system and Python versions, and recent log lines, with your home directory replaced by ~ and command-line arguments, the machine name and local variables removed. An exception message can still name a file or path from the project you were scanning. Nothing is sent unless the CLI crashes. Crash reporting is on by default; aletheore config crash-reporting off (or ALETHEORE_CRASH_REPORTING=0 ) turns it off.
AIR: $29.99/month. Up to 3 team seats, $18 of AI credit a month. Everything in Flash plus the managed dashboard.
